proposed_comments.title: Route property changes to their originating model
proposed_comments.body:
### Route property changes to their originating model

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.JsonRpc/Models/JSPropertyChangeRegistry.cs` (property-change target registration and dispatch).

**Suggested change:** Extend the wire payload with an originating target kind, tag each C# property-change target, and filter dispatch to the matching kind while preserving compatibility for senders without the discriminator. A command item, list item, and nested command can share a `commandId`, so broadcasting every update under that ID lets an icon, title, or command replacement intended for one model mutate the others. Add coverage proving command and item icon updates remain isolated.

confidence.rationale: The registry broadcasts by commandId while distinct live target types intentionally share that ID.

proposed_comments.title: Transmit cleared observable properties
proposed_comments.body:
### Transmit cleared observable properties

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/ts-sdk/src/runtime/runtime.ts` (observable property-change serialization).

**Suggested change:** Serialize an explicit `null` when an optional observable value is assigned `undefined`, while retaining normal serialization for defined values. JSON currently omits undefined object members, so the C# adapter never receives the clear operation and can keep displaying stale state such as an obsolete empty-content command. Add a regression that clears a previously populated optional property.

confidence.rationale: JSON serialization omits undefined members and therefore cannot communicate a clear to the adapter.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve Adaptive Card action IDs on form submission
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve Adaptive Card action IDs on form submission

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.JsonRpc/Models/JSFormContentProxy.cs` and the matching TypeScript form submission runtime/serializer.

**Suggested change:** Implement the action-aware form interface in the C# proxy, include a non-empty `actionId` in `form/submit`, and propagate it through the TypeScript runtime to an optional action handler while retaining the existing `submitForm` fallback. The current bridge sends inputs and data but discards which Adaptive Card action was invoked, so extensions cannot distinguish Save from Cancel. Add C# and SDK tests asserting the action ID reaches the extension.

confidence.rationale: The proxy exposes only the legacy submission shape even though action-aware form events can provide an action ID.

proposed_comments.title: Keep notifications queued until pre-host replay drains
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep notifications queued until pre-host replay drains

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.JsonRpc/Models/JSCommandProviderProxy.cs` (`InitializeWithHost` notification replay).

**Suggested change:** Keep a replacement queue active while replaying, drain repeatedly until it is empty, and only then switch to inline dispatch. The current code marks the queue open before replay finishes, so a newly arriving host notification can execute immediately and overtake an earlier queued show or hide notification. Add a race-focused regression proving a live notification cannot overtake the backlog.

confidence.rationale: The queue is disabled before its backlog is replayed, creating a direct ordering race.

proposed_comments.title: Serialize asynchronous status operations
proposed_comments.body:
### Serialize asynchronous status operations

**Severity:** `high`

**Affected code:** `src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.JsonRpc/Models/JSCommandProviderProxy.cs` (status show, hide, and disposal operations).

**Suggested change:** Queue status operations per provider and await the ordered queue during disposal before releasing host state. The current implementation starts asynchronous `ShowStatus` and `HideStatus` operations independently, so a hide or cleanup can finish before an earlier show and leave stale status visible. Add a regression with a delayed show that verifies the observable order is always show then hide.

confidence.rationale: State tracking is locked but the host-facing asynchronous operations themselves have no ordering primitive.
